newsitem.title: INDONESIA: World Bank pledges to continue aid to Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: World Bank pledges to continue aid to Indonesia.

text.p: The World Bank is committed to continuing its support for Indonesia's development, bank managing-director Gautam Kaji said on Friday.
He said the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) would meet in Japan in July to discuss further assistance for the world's fourth most populous nation.
The CGI, comprising about 17 countries plus financial institutions, pledged $5.26 billion in soft-loan assistance to Indonesia in 1996 compared with $5.35 billion in 1995.
The World Bank's share in 1996 was $1.2 billion, unchanged from the previous year.

"I think the purpose of the consultative group is essentially to try to see whether we can meet the need for Indonesia in term of its development priority and its funding needs," Kaji told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"The bank has always been, shall I say, a significant contributor in that process. We expect to continue to do so," he added.

Indonesia's Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Friday the country was still calculating how much it needed in 1997. "We still need foreign aid, but we are still calculating the amount for 1997," he said.
